svg.title: The carry is a chain, and the chain is the clock
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch building a half adder from an XOR and an AND gate, then a full adder from two half adders and an OR gate, then four full adders wired in a row computing 0111 plus 0001 with the carry drawn as thick red arrows travelling right to left through every stage, and a bar chart comparing ripple-carry gate depth of 19 to 259 against Kogge-Stone depth of 12 to 28 for adders four to sixty-four bits wide.
svg.text: The carry is a chain, and the chain is the clock
THE CHAIN - every carry waits for the one to its right
16-bit ripple: 240 NANDs, depth 67. Kogge-Stone: 503 NANDs, depth 20.
gate DEPTH as the adder gets wider
red = ripple-carry green = Kogge-Stone 9.25x fewer levels at 64 bits
in silicon. You met it in
a signal must pass in ONE tick
